1	# SMA-831: upgrade jiff to 1 as a breaking change of core and the facade
2	
3	Linear: [SMA-831](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-831/upgrade-jiff-to-10-as-a-breaking-change-of-paigasus-helikon-core).
4	Size: a small change. This is the short design.
5	
6	## Intent
7	
8	jiff 1.0.0 was released on 2026-11-15. Dependabot PR #363 bumped the
9	requirement as a `chore(deps)` change, which release-plz releases as a patch.
10	That is wrong: `jiff::Timestamp` is public API of `paigasus-helikon-core`
11	(the `ts` fields of the `SessionEvent` variants, and `SessionEvent::ts()`).
12	A user who passes a jiff 0.2 `Timestamp` in, or passes the returned value to
13	jiff 0.2 code, breaks after the upgrade. The upgrade must be released as a
14	minor bump.
15	
16	## Goals
17	
18	- The workspace requires jiff `1`. `Cargo.lock` has jiff 1.x only.
19	- release-plz makes a **minor** bump of `paigasus-helikon-core` (0.6.0 → 0.7.0).
20	- release-plz makes a **minor** bump of the facade `paigasus-helikon`
21	  (0.6.14 → 0.7.0). The facade re-exports core, so the facade break is the same
22	  break. (Sven's decision, 2026-11-20. It differs from the 0.5 → 0.6 precedent,
23	  where the facade got a patch.)
24	- The CHANGELOGs of core and the facade tell users to upgrade to jiff 1.
25	- A test proves that a sub-second timestamp string that jiff 0.2 wrote still
26	  reads and writes back to the same bytes with jiff 1.
27	- All required CI gates pass.
28	
29	## Non-goals
30	
31	- No minor bump for the other crates that use jiff (evals, runtime-agentcore,
32	  sessions-sqlite, sessions-testkit). They use jiff only internally
33	  (evals `src/run.rs:210`, agentcore `src/a2a/types.rs:51`, testkit
34	  `src/lib.rs:66,217` are all private). They get the normal patch
35	  "update Cargo.toml dependencies".
36	- No change to the general cascade policy (dependents of a core minor get a
37	  patch). That is a separate question.
38	- No move of jiff from `[dependencies]` to `[dev-dependencies]` in
39	  sessions-sqlite, although its `src/` does not use jiff. Separate cleanup.
40	- No fix for the five `trybuild_ui` mismatches in core. They fail the same way
41	  on clean `main` with local rustc 1.99.0, and they are not from this change.
42	- No fix of the `dependencies_update` comment in `release-plz.toml`.
43	
44	## Anti-goals
45	
46	- The release PR shows a patch bump of core or the facade.
47	- Any crate other than core and the facade gets a minor bump.
48	- The JSON format of a stored `SessionEvent` changes, so old session rows
49	  cannot be read.
50	
51	## Constraints and facts found
52	
53	- A probe compiled the whole workspace (`--all-features --all-targets`) with
54	  jiff 1.0.1 and no source change. The lockfile moved jiff, jiff-core,
55	  jiff-static to 1.0.1 and jiff-tzdb, jiff-tzdb-platform to 1.0.0.
56	- The core `serde_roundtrip` snapshot tests pass with jiff 1. But they use only
57	  `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`, so they do not prove the sub-second case. Real rows
58	  hold `Timestamp::now()` values with nanoseconds.
59	- jiff-static 1.0 pulls `syn` 3.x next to `syn` 2.x. `deny.toml` has
60	  `[bans] multiple-versions = "warn"`, so `deny` does not fail on it.
61	- jiff 1.0 needs Rust 1.85. The workspace MSRV is 1.94.
62	- release-plz gives a commit to a crate only when the commit changes files in
63	  that crate's directory. A change to the root `Cargo.toml` alone gives no
64	  commit to core.
65	- On a 0.x crate, release-plz turns a breaking commit (`!` after the type, or a
66	  `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) into a minor bump, and a `feat` into a patch.
67	  Precedent: `feat(runtime)!: SMA-482 …` (#177) gave runtime-actix,
68	  runtime-axum and runtime-agentcore 0.1.x → 0.2.0, and the facade
69	  0.4.26 → 0.5.0. No precedent has `chore!`, so step 6 must prove it.
70	- The repo sets `squash_merge_commit_title = PR_TITLE` and
71	  `squash_merge_commit_message = BLANK`. The squash commit on `main` is thus
72	  exactly the PR title plus ` (#N)`, with no body. Only the `!` in the title can
73	  carry the breaking marker; a footer cannot.
74	- `convco check` accepts `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1`. The
75	  `pr-title` regex (`pr-title.yml:85`) accepts the subject, and earlier `!`
76	  titles passed the gate.
77	- CI installs the release-plz CLI **v0.4.3** (release-plz run 44807764156).
78	  The local copy is 0.3.158, so it is not a valid stand-in.
79	- release-plz keeps hand-written text under `## [Unreleased]` and moves it into
80	  the release section (precedent: PR #351, the `### Security` notes).
81	- SMA-810 and SMA-826 are on `main` and not yet released for core. They join
82	  core 0.7.0.
83	- Nothing publishes until the release PR merges (`release-plz.yml:51-62`).
84	
85	## Approaches
86	
87	- **A. Breaking marker on the squash commit (picked).** The PR title is
88	  `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1`. The upgrade notes in the core and
89	  facade CHANGELOGs make the commit touch both crate directories, so release-plz
90	  gives the breaking commit to exactly these two crates. Risk: if the `!` is
91	  removed from the title before the merge, the bump falls back to a patch.
92	  Step 8 catches that before anything publishes.
93	- **B. Hand-bump core and the facade to 0.7.0 in the PR.** Rejected. SMA-622
94	  used a hand bump for `runtime-temporal`, but that crate has only the facade
95	  as a dependent. Core has about 17 dependents. The release-plz cascade does
96	  not run for a hand bump, so each dependent's pin and version need hand edits,
97	  and the PR publishes on its own merge.
98	- **C. Rely on cargo-semver-checks.** Rejected: it is not certain that it
99	  detects a major-version change of a type from a dependency.
100	
101	## Design
102	
103	1. **Compatibility test first, on jiff 0.2.** Add a core test that
104	   deserializes a `SessionEvent` whose `ts` is a sub-second RFC 3339 string in
105	   the form jiff 0.2 writes (for example `2026-11-20T15:08:42.123456789Z`), and
106	   asserts that serializing it again gives the same bytes. Take the literal from
107	   real jiff 0.2 output on `main`. The test must pass before the upgrade, and
108	   again after it.
109	2. Root `Cargo.toml`: `jiff = { version = "1", features = ["serde"] }`. Replace
110	   the comment above it. Keep the SMA-818 reason (a caret requirement, not an
111	   exact pin). Drop the 0.2.29 / RUSTSEC-2026-0173 history, because it applies
112	   only to 0.2. Keep the statement that `jiff::Timestamp` is public API of core,
113	   so the next jiff major is a breaking change of core and the facade.
114	3. `cargo update -p jiff` so the lockfile has jiff 1.x only.
115	4. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md` and
116	   `crates/paigasus-helikon/CHANGELOG.md`: add an `### Upgrade notes` section
117	   under `## [Unreleased]`. The note says:
118	   - the `ts` fields of `SessionEvent` and `SessionEvent::ts()` now use
119	     `jiff::Timestamp` from jiff 1;
120	   - code that passes a `Timestamp` in or uses the returned value with jiff
121	     code must change its `jiff` requirement to `1`;
122	   - code that uses only the constructors that set `ts` to now (for example
123	     `SessionEvent::user_message`) and does not read `ts` needs no change;
124	   - upgrade core and the facade together, and upgrade them to 0.7. If the
125	     lockfile still holds facade 0.6 after a `cargo update`, it can hold two
126	     copies of core. Check with `cargo tree -d`;
127	   - the stored JSON format does not change, so old rows stay readable;
128	   - link the jiff 1.0 changelog for the APIs that jiff itself renamed.
129	5. mdBook and READMEs: the only jiff reference is
130	   `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md` (`ts: jiff::Timestamp`), with no
131	   version. It stays correct. No README mentions jiff. No edit.
132	6. **Verify the bump before the PR.** In a scratch clone with all tags, squash
133	   the branch onto current `origin/main` as one commit with the message
134	   `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1 (#999)` and no body. Install
135	   release-plz v0.4.3 and cargo-semver-checks into a scratch root. Run
136	   `release-plz update` and check the full version table: core and the facade
137	   go to 0.7.0, every other changed crate gets a patch, no other crate gets a
138	   minor, and the `[Unreleased]` notes move into the 0.7.0 sections.
139	7. **Allowed diff.** The branch changes only the root `Cargo.toml`,
140	   `Cargo.lock`, the two CHANGELOGs, the new core test file (inside
141	   `crates/paigasus-helikon-core`, so it adds no other crate) and
142	   `docs/superpowers/`. Each branch commit that touches a CHANGELOG also uses a
143	   `!` type. The PR title is `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1`, and the
144	   PR body says that the `!` drives the minor bump and must stay in the title.
145	8. **Check after the merge.** Before anyone merges the release PR, confirm
146	   that it shows core 0.7.0 and facade 0.7.0. If it shows patches, do not merge
147	   it. Recover with a follow-up `chore(deps)!:` PR that touches both
148	   CHANGELOGs.
149	
150	## Left to the builder
151	
152	- The exact wording of the comment and the CHANGELOG notes (ASD-STE100 style).
153	- How to set up the scratch clone for step 6.
154	- Dependabot can open a new jiff PR on Monday 06:00 UTC. If this PR is not
155	  merged by then, close the Dependabot PR. After the merge, the requirement is
156	  `1`, so Dependabot does not propose jiff 1.0 again.

# SMA-831: upgrade jiff to 1 as a breaking change of core and the facade

Linear: [SMA-831](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-831/upgrade-jiff-to-10-as-a-breaking-change-of-paigasus-helikon-core).
Size: a small change. This is the short design.

## Intent

jiff 1.0.0 was released on 2026-11-15. Dependabot PR #363 bumped the
requirement as a `chore(deps)` change, which release-plz releases as a patch.
That is wrong: `jiff::Timestamp` is public API of `paigasus-helikon-core`
(the `ts` fields of the `SessionEvent` variants, and `SessionEvent::ts()`).
A user who passes a jiff 0.2 `Timestamp` in, or passes the returned value to
jiff 0.2 code, breaks after the upgrade. The upgrade must be released as a
minor bump.

## Goals

- The workspace requires jiff `1`. `Cargo.lock` has jiff 1.x only.
- release-plz makes a **minor** bump of `paigasus-helikon-core` (0.6.0 → 0.7.0).
- release-plz makes a **minor** bump of the facade `paigasus-helikon`
  (0.6.14 → 0.7.0). The facade re-exports core, so the facade break is the same
  break. (Sven's decision, 2026-11-20. It differs from the 0.5 → 0.6 precedent,
  where the facade got a patch.)
- The CHANGELOGs of core and the facade tell users to upgrade to jiff 1.
- A test proves that a sub-second timestamp string that jiff 0.2 wrote still
  reads and writes back to the same bytes with jiff 1.
- All required CI gates pass.

## Non-goals

- No minor bump for the other crates that use jiff (evals, runtime-agentcore,
  sessions-sqlite, sessions-testkit). They use jiff only internally
  (evals `src/run.rs:210`, agentcore `src/a2a/types.rs:51`, testkit
  `src/lib.rs:66,217` are all private). They get the normal patch
  "update Cargo.toml dependencies".
- No change to the general cascade policy (dependents of a core minor get a
  patch). That is a separate question.
- No move of jiff from `[dependencies]` to `[dev-dependencies]` in
  sessions-sqlite, although its `src/` does not use jiff. Separate cleanup.
- No fix for the five `trybuild_ui` mismatches in core. They fail the same way
  on clean `main` with local rustc 1.99.0, and they are not from this change.
- No fix of the `dependencies_update` comment in `release-plz.toml`.

## Anti-goals

- The release PR shows a patch bump of core or the facade.
- Any crate other than core and the facade gets a minor bump.
- The JSON format of a stored `SessionEvent` changes, so old session rows
  cannot be read.

## Constraints and facts found

  jiff 1.0.1 and no source change. The lockfile moved jiff, jiff-core,
  jiff-static to 1.0.1 and jiff-tzdb, jiff-tzdb-platform to 1.0.0.
- The core `serde_roundtrip` snapshot tests pass with jiff 1. But they use only
  `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`, so they do not prove the sub-second case. Real rows
  hold `Timestamp::now()` values with nanoseconds.
- jiff-static 1.0 pulls `syn` 3.x next to `syn` 2.x. `deny.toml` has
  `[bans] multiple-versions = "warn"`, so `deny` does not fail on it.
- jiff 1.0 needs Rust 1.85. The workspace MSRV is 1.94.
- release-plz gives a commit to a crate only when the commit changes files in
  that crate's directory. A change to the root `Cargo.toml` alone gives no
  commit to core.
- On a 0.x crate, release-plz turns a breaking commit (`!` after the type, or a
  `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) into a minor bump, and a `feat` into a patch.
  Precedent: `feat(runtime)!: SMA-482 …` (#177) gave runtime-actix,
  runtime-axum and runtime-agentcore 0.1.x → 0.2.0, and the facade
  0.4.26 → 0.5.0. No precedent has `chore!`, so step 6 must prove it.
- The repo sets `squash_merge_commit_title = PR_TITLE` and
  `squash_merge_commit_message = BLANK`. The squash commit on `main` is thus
  exactly the PR title plus ` (#N)`, with no body. Only the `!` in the title can
  carry the breaking marker; a footer cannot.
- `convco check` accepts `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1`. The
  `pr-title` regex (`pr-title.yml:85`) accepts the subject, and earlier `!`
  titles passed the gate.
- CI installs the release-plz CLI **v0.4.3** (release-plz run 44807764156).
  The local copy is 0.3.158, so it is not a valid stand-in.
- release-plz keeps hand-written text under `## [Unreleased]` and moves it into
  the release section (precedent: PR #351, the `### Security` notes).
- SMA-810 and SMA-826 are on `main` and not yet released for core. They join
  core 0.7.0.
- Nothing publishes until the release PR merges (`release-plz.yml:51-62`).

- **A. Breaking marker on the squash commit (picked).** The PR title is

  gives the breaking commit to exactly these two crates. Risk: if the `!` is
  removed from the title before the merge, the bump falls back to a patch.
  Step 8 catches that before anything publishes.
- **B. Hand-bump core and the facade to 0.7.0 in the PR.** Rejected. SMA-622
  used a hand bump for `runtime-temporal`, but that crate has only the facade
  as a dependent. Core has about 17 dependents. The release-plz cascade does
  not run for a hand bump, so each dependent's pin and version need hand edits,
  and the PR publishes on its own merge.
- **C. Rely on cargo-semver-checks.** Rejected: it is not certain that it
  detects a major-version change of a type from a dependency.

## Design

1. **Compatibility test first, on jiff 0.2.** Add a core test that
   deserializes a `SessionEvent` whose `ts` is a sub-second RFC 3339 string in
   the form jiff 0.2 writes (for example `2026-11-20T15:08:42.123456789Z`), and
   asserts that serializing it again gives the same bytes. Take the literal from
   real jiff 0.2 output on `main`. The test must pass before the upgrade, and
   again after it.
2. Root `Cargo.toml`: `jiff = { version = "1", features = ["serde"] }`. Replace
   the comment above it. Keep the SMA-818 reason (a caret requirement, not an
   exact pin). Drop the 0.2.29 / RUSTSEC-2026-0173 history, because it applies
   only to 0.2. Keep the statement that `jiff::Timestamp` is public API of core,
   so the next jiff major is a breaking change of core and the facade.
3. `cargo update -p jiff` so the lockfile has jiff 1.x only.
4. `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md` and
   `crates/paigasus-helikon/CHANGELOG.md`: add an `### Upgrade notes` section
   under `## [Unreleased]`. The note says:
   - the `ts` fields of `SessionEvent` and `SessionEvent::ts()` now use
     `jiff::Timestamp` from jiff 1;
   - code that passes a `Timestamp` in or uses the returned value with jiff
     code must change its `jiff` requirement to `1`;
   - code that uses only the constructors that set `ts` to now (for example
     `SessionEvent::user_message`) and does not read `ts` needs no change;
   - upgrade core and the facade together, and upgrade them to 0.7. If the
     lockfile still holds facade 0.6 after a `cargo update`, it can hold two
     copies of core. Check with `cargo tree -d`;
   - the stored JSON format does not change, so old rows stay readable;
   - link the jiff 1.0 changelog for the APIs that jiff itself renamed.
5. mdBook and READMEs: the only jiff reference is
   `docs/book/src/concepts/sessions.md` (`ts: jiff::Timestamp`), with no
   version. It stays correct. No README mentions jiff. No edit.
6. **Verify the bump before the PR.** In a scratch clone with all tags, squash
   the branch onto current `origin/main` as one commit with the message
   `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1 (#999)` and no body. Install
   release-plz v0.4.3 and cargo-semver-checks into a scratch root. Run
   `release-plz update` and check the full version table: core and the facade
   go to 0.7.0, every other changed crate gets a patch, no other crate gets a
   minor, and the `[Unreleased]` notes move into the 0.7.0 sections.
7. **Allowed diff.** The branch changes only the root `Cargo.toml`,
   `Cargo.lock`, the two CHANGELOGs, the new core test file (inside
   `crates/paigasus-helikon-core`, so it adds no other crate) and
   `docs/superpowers/`. Each branch commit that touches a CHANGELOG also uses a
   `!` type. The PR title is `chore(deps)!: SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1`, and the
   PR body says that the `!` drives the minor bump and must stay in the title.
8. **Check after the merge.** Before anyone merges the release PR, confirm
   that it shows core 0.7.0 and facade 0.7.0. If it shows patches, do not merge
   it. Recover with a follow-up `chore(deps)!:` PR that touches both
   CHANGELOGs.

## Left to the builder

- The exact wording of the comment and the CHANGELOG notes (ASD-STE100 style).
- How to set up the scratch clone for step 6.
- Dependabot can open a new jiff PR on Monday 06:00 UTC. If this PR is not
  merged by then, close the Dependabot PR. After the merge, the requirement is
  `1`, so Dependabot does not propose jiff 1.0 again.

104	- release-plz publishes in **dependency order: core → tools → facade**, so `tools`'s verify runs against the fresh `core` on the registry. No deadlock; the cascade stays intact so **no facade drift**.
105	
106	No manual version edits, no manual `[workspace.dependencies]` pin edits, no hand-written CHANGELOG entries — release-plz owns all of it. **Reactive fallback only:** if a publish step unexpectedly deadlocks, fix it with a follow-up `chore(release): SMA-418 …` PR (the proven SMA-321/SMA-346 pattern). This is also why the squashed PR commit is a real `feat` (proper changelog entry for the new public method), not a `chore`.

108	(Versions above are the values current on `main` as of this design; release-plz reads whatever is current at release time.)

300	//! window from the activity's full `start_to_close` timeout (default 300s) down to roughly
301	//! `2 × interval`. **Recommendation: offload blocking or CPU-bound tool work via
302	//! `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`** so the executor keeps polling the heartbeat ticker. This
303	//! interacts directly with the **tool idempotency under crash-retry** warning above — enabling
304	//! heartbeats is a latency/reclamation *tuning* choice with that trade-off, not a free win.
305	//!
306	//! # Payload Budget and Conversation Size
307	//!
308	//! The durable driver builds every `ModelRequest` from the **full conversation** — including all
309	//! history since the run started. This means each `call_model` activity payload includes the
310	//! entire conversation-so-far, causing payload size to grow quadratically with the number of turns.
311	//! Temporal's default gRPC payload limit is ~2–4 MB, with server-side warnings around 512 KB.
312	//!
313	//! **Practical budget for v0:** A single activity payload should stay under **~1.5 MB of JSON**.
314	//! This typically allows **15–20 turns** with tool outputs averaging **≤50 KB each**. A single
315	//! tool result larger than ~1.5 MB will fail its activity outright.
316	//!
317	//! **Strategies to fit within the budget:**
318	//! - Bound tool output size via the tool implementation (e.g., truncate summaries, paginate results).
319	//! - Limit `max_turns` in [`RunConfig`](paigasus_helikon_core::RunConfig) to stay within the turn budget.
320	//! - Monitor your actual payload sizes in Temporal's Web UI to verify your use case fits.
321	//!
322	//! **The `Ctx` seed adds to this budget too.** When a client sets
323	//! [`runner::TemporalRunnerConfig::with_ctx_seed`], that seed is serialized into the activity
324	//! input on **every** `render_instructions` and `invoke_tool` call (once per turn and once per
325	//! tool call, not once per run) — keep it small (ids, claims), not bulk data.
326	//!
327	//! Payload codecs (custom serialization), claim-check blob offloading, and conversation
328	//! compaction are named follow-up work, not silent gaps.
329	//!
330	//! # Upgrade Discipline and Determinism
331	//!
332	//! The workflow's deterministic core is [`paigasus_helikon_core::loop_state::transition`], which
333	//! lives in a separately versioned crate. Replaying an in-flight workflow against a worker with a
334	//! **different version of `paigasus-helikon-core` or `paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal`** can
335	//! cause non-determinism errors (the workflow's replayed decisions don't match the new code's
336	//! logic).
337	//!
338	//! **Activity input encoding is not a replay hazard.** Temporal's replay check compares an
339	//! activity's **id** and **type** only — never its input payloads
340	//! (`temporalio-sdk-core-0.9.0`, `activity_state_machine.rs`, the
341	//! `IdAndTypeDeterminismChecks` gate). Changing how an activity's arguments are encoded
342	//! therefore cannot trip the non-determinism checker; *renaming* an activity would. This
343	//! statement is pinned to `temporalio-* = 1.0.0` / `temporalio-sdk-core = 0.9.0` and must
344	//! be re-verified on any SDK bump.
345	//! (Re-verified for 1.0 in SMA-622: `on_activity_task_scheduled` in
346	//! `temporalio-sdk-core-0.9.0` is byte-identical to the 0.7.0 body and still compares only
347	//! `act_id`/`activity_id` and `act_type`/`activity_type`, never payloads. Activity and
348	//! workflow *type names* are derived unchanged as well
349	//! (`temporalio-macros-1.0.0/src/activities_definitions.rs:548`,
350	//! `workflow_definitions.rs:644-647`), so registered names are stable across the bump —
351	//! which is what makes this guarantee useful rather than merely true.
352	//! Previously re-verified for 0.7 in SMA-549.)
353	//!
354	//! **A mixed 0.7/1.0 worker fleet is not proven safe.** The two properties above are
355	//! established: input encoding is not a replay hazard, and activity/workflow type names
356	//! do not move. Beyond them, nothing in CI exercises a 1.0 worker replaying a history
357	//! written by a 0.7 worker — `temporal-it` starts a fresh server, so it only ever replays
358	//! its own 1.0 histories. Prefer draining in-flight runs across this upgrade, or use a
359	//! blue-green task queue, exactly as for the 0.5.0 envelope change below.
360	//!
361	//! **SMA-484 wire change (activity inputs are envelope-only as of 0.3.0).** Each of
362	//! `render_instructions` / `call_model` / `invoke_tool` takes one self-describing JSON-object
363	//! payload, and that is now the **only** shape a worker decodes. The pre-envelope positional
364	//! shapes (0.2.1 and earlier) are recognized solely to produce a named decode error; SMA-462's
365	//! 0.2.2 release, which decoded both, is the migration bridge **for 0.2.0 and 0.2.1**. 0.1.x
366	//! remains outside the support window and fails closed as before — see the 0.1.x note below,
367	//! because the bridge does not rescue it.
368	//!
369	//! **Upgrading from 0.2.0 or 0.2.1 requires a stop at 0.2.2**, for activity inputs:
370	//!
371	//! | from → to | outcome |
372	//! |---|---|
373	//! | `0.2.2` → `0.3.0` | compatible **both** ways — both encode and decode the envelope; no drain needed for this change |
374	//! | `0.2.0` / `0.2.1` → `0.3.0`, directly | **broken both ways** — `0.3.0` cannot read legacy-queued tasks, and a `0.2.0`/`0.2.1` worker cannot read an envelope |
375	//! | `0.2.0` / `0.2.1` → `0.2.2` → `0.3.0` | works, **provided in-flight runs are drained while the fleet is on 0.2.2** |
376	//!
377	//! **0.1.x cannot use the bridge.** 0.2.2 decodes the 0.2.0/0.2.1 arities specifically, and only
378	//! `call_model`'s shape (2 payloads) happens to be unchanged since 0.1.x. A 0.1.x
379	//! `render_instructions` task is one payload and fails in 0.2.2's envelope arm; a 0.1.x
380	//! `invoke_tool` task is two payloads, which is not `invoke_tool`'s legacy arity, so it fails
381	//! there too. A fleet on 0.1.x must therefore drain (or terminate) its in-flight runs outright
382	//! rather than hopping through 0.2.2. Note the *diagnostic* wording stays "0.2.1 and earlier"
383	//! deliberately: it describes the shape that arrived, and `call_model`'s 2-payload shape really
384	//! does date back to 0.1.x.
385	//!
386	//! Throughout this section, *drain* means: stop starting new executions on the task queue, and
387	//! wait until every execution already on it reaches a **terminal** state — not merely pausing
388	//! new runs.
389	//!
390	//! **If a 0.3.0 worker meets a pre-envelope task anyway**, it logs at `ERROR` and fails the
391	//! attempt **retryably**, so Temporal re-dispatches. That is the recovery path: any worker on
392	//! 0.2.2 still polling the queue decodes and executes the task, for as long as 0.2.2 can still
393	//! decode the nested core types in play (see the field-evolution scope below). Re-join one, let
394	//! in-flight runs drain, then remove it. 0.2.2 and 0.3.0 share identical workflow logic, so a
395	//! temporary mixed fleet across this pair is not a replay hazard; the one-version-at-a-time rule
396	//! above still governs every other pair. A run that cannot be drained in an acceptable window is
397	//! handled with a blue-green task queue (below) or by terminating the execution.
398	//!
399	//! **The envelope is unreadable below 0.2.2, and that matters during a rolling deploy.** A
400	//! **0.2.1-and-earlier** worker handed an envelope payload cannot decode it. It fails the
401	//! attempt retryably and Temporal re-dispatches until a worker that understands the envelope
402	//! takes it. The same is true of a 0.3.0 worker handed a pre-envelope payload. Four things bound
403	//! that recovery:
404	//!
405	//! 1. A finite `maximum_attempts` on `model_retry_policy` / `tool_retry_policy` can be exhausted.
406	//! 2. `WorkflowInput::timeout_ms` interrupts the whole run on its own schedule, regardless of
407	//!    retry policy.
408	//! 3. A terminal `render_instructions` failure ends the run; it is not a degraded step.
409	//! 4. Exhausted `invoke_tool` retries are folded into a tool-error result and fed to the model
410	//!    rather than failing loudly.
411	//!
412	//! **Neither of the first two is on by default.** `render_instructions` is built with no retry
413	//! policy at all, so the Temporal server default — unlimited attempts — applies; and
414	//! `WorkflowInput::timeout_ms` is `None` unless set, meaning no deadline. On a default
415	//! configuration the retry loop is therefore **unbounded**: the run retries indefinitely, writing
416	//! one `ActivityTaskFailed` event per attempt and consuming workflow history. Do not rely on the
417	//! failure self-terminating; recovery is operator action.
418	//!
419	//! So: **keep the mixed-fleet window short**, and either drain in-flight runs first or ensure
420	//! retry caps are unlimited and run deadlines generous for the duration of the rollout.
421	//!
422	//! **Rolling back.** Once a worker has queued an envelope-shaped activity task, that payload is
423	//! frozen in the `ActivityTaskScheduled` event and every retry re-delivers it. A rollback to
424	//! **below 0.2.2** leaves those activities undecodable until the run deadline — which, on a
425	//! default configuration, does not exist. **Drain in-flight runs before rolling back below 0.2.2.**
426	//! Rolling back from 0.3.0 to 0.2.2 is safe: 0.2.2 decodes the envelope.
427	//!
428	//! **What this buys.** Future additive changes to an activity's input are compatible in both
429	//! directions, because the envelope is self-describing: unknown fields are ignored and absent
430	//! fields default. That guarantee is scoped to **the envelope's own field set**. It does *not*
431	//! extend to the `paigasus-helikon-core` types nested inside those envelopes (`ModelRequest`,
432	//! `ToolCallRequest`), nor to activity **outputs** — a serde change in any of those breaks the
433	//! wire exactly as before.
434	//!
435	//! **Operational guidance:**
436	//!
437	//! 1. **Upgrade one release at a time.** Skipping a release skips the overlap window in which
438	//!    both shapes are readable (a fleet on 0.2.0 or 0.2.1 goes → 0.2.2 → 0.3.0, draining while
439	//!    on 0.2.2; 0.1.x has no such overlap and must drain outright).
440	//! 2. **Drain in-flight runs before redeploying** when in doubt. Agent runs are typically
441	//!    minutes-to-hours, not months. Alternatively use blue-green task queues: point the old
442	//!    worker to `"queue-v1"` and the runner to `"queue-v2"`, run new workflows on v2 while old
443	//!    ones drain from v1, then decommission v1.
444	//! 3. **Check the CHANGELOG.** Any release whose transition behavior changed is flagged as
445	//!    replay-breaking.
446	//! 4. **Production path:** [Temporal Worker Versioning (Build IDs)](https://docs.temporal.io/workers#worker-versioning)
447	//!    is the long-term solution for zero-downtime updates; support is pending in the Rust SDK.
448	//!

34	- **`RunContext<Ctx>`** — the per-run state shared across loop, tools, guardrails, and hooks (user context, `Session` handle, `HookRegistry`, `TracerHandle`, `CancellationToken`). Build with `RunContext::new(user_ctx, session, hooks, tracer, cancel)` (all five arguments explicit) or use `RunContext::ephemeral(user_ctx)` as the shorthand for the all-defaults case (in-memory session, empty hooks, default tracer, fresh cancel token); individual parts can then be overridden with the consuming setters `.with_session(...)`, `.with_hooks(...)`, `.with_tracer(...)`, `.with_cancel(...)`. **`RunConfig`** carries per-run knobs (`max_turns`, `timeout`, `parallel_tool_call_limit`, `max_agent_depth`). **`RunResult<T>`** (and its streaming counterpart `RunResultStreaming`) aggregate the run's `final_output`, `events`, and `TokenUsage`.

    - The wire canary `call_model_decodes_frozen_envelope_literal` (activity_input.rs:777-791) uses `"tools":[]`. It cannot detect any `ToolDef` wire change.
  - **Suggested fix.**
    1. Replace the `AgentPlan` example with the `call_model` activity input.
    2. Add a frozen-literal test in activity_input.rs with one old-shape `ToolDef` and one `ToolDef` with `provider_types`.
    3. Add a runtime-temporal CHANGELOG note: a mixed fleet is safe, but it silently falls back to the generic entry.
    4. Extend `register_accepts_plain_agent_and_snapshots_tool_defs` (worker.rs:767) to assert that `provider_types` survive `register()`.

- **The spec has no upgrade notes.**
  - **What is wrong.** The Design section has no CHANGELOG work. SMA-831 wrote explicit notes (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-830/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/CHANGELOG.md:22-29`).
  - **Why it matters.** Downstream `ToolDef { .. }` literals and exhaustive destructuring stop compiling. A downstream `Tool` decorator inherits the default `&[]` and silently drops the declaration. Users with mixed core versions get "trait not implemented" errors.
  - **Suggested fix.** Add a "CHANGELOG upgrade notes" step for core and the facade. Cover these points:
    - Use `ToolDef::new` or `ToolDef::from_tool`.
    - Exhaustive destructuring is no longer possible.
    - Upgrade core, the facade and the direct dependents together, and check with `cargo tree -d`.
    - A tool wrapper must forward `provider_types`.
    - The Temporal mixed-fleet behaviour.
    - The stored JSON does not change.
  - Also put the "forward `provider_types`" rule in the `///` comment of `Tool::provider_types`.

- **The claim "GA, needs no `anthropic-beta` header" is not verified, and the feature depends on it.**
  - **What is wrong.** Spec:154 gives no evidence. The memory tool shipped as a beta behind `context-management-2025-06-27`. Spec:151 also claims without evidence that the API accepts `cache_control` on a typed entry.
  - **Why it matters.** If the header is still necessary, every request that has the typed entry fails with 400. The project rule (memory `feedback_verify_provider_wire_with_container`) is to verify wire formats from traces, not from vendor docs.
  - **Suggested fix.**
    1. Before implementation, capture one live request that has the typed entry plus `cache_control`. Record the result in the spec.
    2. Add an env-gated case in `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-830/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/live.rs`.
    3. If a header is necessary, document `.beta(...)` (`/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-830/crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/src/builder.rs:116`).

- **The declaration is static and cannot follow the model, and there is no opt-out.**
  - **What is wrong.** `Tool::provider_types()` cannot see the model. "First `anthropic` entry wins" (spec:140) means one tool sends the same typed entry to every Anthropic model and to every `base_url` endpoint (builder.rs:103).
  - Anthropic client tool types depend on the model: the `text_editor` version and its required name change between model generations, and memory works only on newer models. So the claim "covers every Anthropic client tool" (spec:68) is too strong.
  - **Why it matters.** An older model, or an Anthropic-compatible gateway, returns 400 on every turn. The host can only fall back if it removes the declaration from the tool.
  - **Suggested fix (choose one).**
    - Add `AnthropicModelBuilder::native_tool_types(bool)` (default `true`) to force the generic entry.
    - Document the limitation and change the claim to "one type per tool per provider, sent to every model".

## What's good
- The anti-goals are precise and the design meets them. `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]` keeps today's bytes and reads old JSON.
- `ToolDef::from_tool` removes the duplicated mapping at `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-830/crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/agent.rs:907-914` and `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.claude/worktrees/sma-830/crates/paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal/src/worker.rs:396-404`. `#[non_exhaustive]` makes later `ToolDef` fields non-breaking.
- The carrier is provider-agnostic (a provider string plus a params map). Each provider gets a fallback test. "type/name set last" is a correct guard. The translation is a pure function (`translate_tools`), so it is easy to test.
